51.name: Lium
51.product: GPU rental marketplace (H100/H200/B200), about 1,600 GPUs listed, roughly 90% rented
51.revenue: Run rate about $12–16M/yr (Oct 2026); last month's billing $1.3M, 3× year on year
51.buyback_detail: Revenue buys and burns SN51 alpha: over $2.7M in about 6 months, nearly $1M in one September transaction
51.price_vs_web2: H100 about $1.50/h vs RunPod $2.69, Lambda $3.99, AWS $8+ (Aug 2026); H200 about $1.74 vs RunPod $3.99
51.key_risk: Valuation needs far more revenue; billing data no longer public since Oct 2026

4.name: Targon
4.product: Confidential GPU/CPU VMs, bare metal, sandboxes and inference (Intel TDX, NVIDIA CC)
4.revenue: Self-reported about $10.4M ARR (Sept 2025, unaudited); about $100K/month in a July 2025 interview; no public dashboard
4.buyback_detail: Revenue-funded buybacks: over 2,000 TAO (May 2026) and over 550 TAO (Aug 2026)
4.price_vs_web2: Team claims about 85% cheaper than AWS (2025, unverified); no public list prices
4.key_risk: Revenue unaudited and far below emissions; customers mostly Bittensor projects (Dippy, Ridges, Score)

41.name: Almanac
41.product: Polymarket trading terminal with 1% trading fee plus crowd forecasting
41.revenue: Over $20M traded through the terminal (about half in the 30 days to mid-Oct 2026); at 1% fee roughly $200K in fees (derived)
41.buyback_detail: Monthly alpha buybacks, mostly burned: over $160,000 since Feb 2026
41.price_vs_web2: No price comparison; Almanac sits on top of Polymarket
41.key_risk: Founder sold about 3,000 TAO of alpha in Feb 2026; depends on Polymarket

93.name: Bitcast
93.product: Brands pay creators via campaigns ('briefs') on YouTube and X; several apps built on SN93
93.revenue: Brand payments offset miner emissions; 'strong revenue' (Aug 2026) without figures; part of the $19M/yr dashboard sum
93.buyback_detail: Revenue funds alpha buybacks and burns; manual burn of about $630K alpha; offsets emissions since Aug 2026
93.key_risk: Engagement-based rewards can be gamed; client base mostly crypto projects

53.name: engy
53.product: Inference API for open models (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi), sold directly
53.revenue: Not disclosed; claims 100% month-on-month growth (Oct 2026); about 49M requests in 30 days, over 50B tokens on one day
53.buyback_detail: Buybacks since 12 Aug 2026: 25,287 alpha burned (about $214K) by 25 Oct 2026
53.price_vs_web2: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.03/$0.12 per M tokens; no direct web2 comparison published
53.key_risk: Usage figures self-reported; small team (Hanlin AI) also runs SN11

28.name: GM
28.product: Private (TEE) gateway to Claude, GPT and Gemini, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API, about 70 models
28.buyback_detail: Cycle 1 burned $43,088 (12.9% of miner emissions), cycle 2 $104,372 (20.3%)
28.price_vs_web2: Capped at provider list prices, often below; one client about 12% below Anthropic list price
28.key_risk: Burns cover only about a fifth of emissions so far

56.name: Gradients
56.product: No-code model training and fine-tuning (gradients.io + SDK), $10–50/hour
56.buyback_detail: Tournament fees fund buy-and-burns: 103 TAO (Jan), 164 TAO (Apr), 268 TAO (Sep 2026)
56.web2_competitors: Together AI, Google Vertex, AWS SageMaker
56.price_vs_web2: Self-reported about 26% cheaper than Together AI; $100–500 per run vs $10,000+ on Vertex (multiple sources)
56.key_risk: Performance and cost claims self-reported; Rayon Labs emissions share fell sharply in 2026

64.name: Chutes
64.product: Serverless AI inference, about 490 models, OpenRouter's largest open-source provider by tokens
64.revenue: Estimates range from about $0.6M to $8M/yr (Pine $1.3–2.4M; author measurement $0.6–3.7M); team withdrew its revenue series in mid-2026
64.buyback_detail: No explicit buyback; revenue reportedly auto-stakes into alpha
64.web2_competitors: OpenRouter providers, Together AI, Fireworks, AWS Bedrock
64.price_vs_web2: Budget models $0.025–0.10/M vs Together $0.10–0.50, Fireworks $0.10–0.30, Bedrock $0.15–1.00 (Aug 2026); unsubsidised break-even about $1.41/M, i.e. 1.6–3.5× more expensive than centralised
64.key_risk: Prices subsidised by emissions; emission share falling (14% → 6%)

44.name: Score
44.product: Football video analytics and vision AI (Score Studio, Manako at 20 AVIA stations)
44.revenue: First break-even month Sept 2026; two long-term paying private-track clients; recurring five-figure invoice
44.buyback_detail: About 20% of revenue guided to buybacks/burns (2025), not yet formalised
44.price_vs_web2: Plans $69 and $249/month; claims about 10× cheaper than centralised stacks; Hawk-Eye-type systems $500K–1M+ per venue
44.key_risk: Revenue concentrated in a few clients; small team

19.name: blockmachine
19.product: Paid blockchain RPC service across 11 chains, $9–999/month plans
19.revenue: Not disclosed; Taostats sends about 15B requests/month, 65B requests served by Sept 2026
19.buyback_detail: Monthly buybacks scaled to paid traffic, burned: 9,797 alpha (about $24K) in six cycles May–Oct 2026
19.key_risk: Small buyback size; depends heavily on Taostats traffic

75.name: Hippius
75.product: S3-compatible decentralised storage plus IPFS; Hippius Drive
75.revenue: Not disclosed; storage fees described as minimal/early
75.web2_competitors: AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Filecoin
75.price_vs_web2: $6 per TB/month with no egress fees vs AWS S3 Standard about $23 per TB/month plus egress
75.key_risk: Top 10 wallets hold about 61%; revenue minimal

48.name: Quantum Compute
48.product: Marketplace for quantum compute tasks; runs over 90% of Open Quantum traffic
48.revenue: Not disclosed; active users +206% in summer 2026
48.buyback_detail: Revenue-funded buybacks announced to start Oct 2026
48.price_vs_web2: About half of vendor price: $0.18 (public) / $0.36 (private) per task
48.key_risk: Early; miner onboarding still in progress

8.name: Vanta
8.product: Decentralised prop-trading evaluation platform (fees $199/$349/$549), Glitch Financial app

110.name: Green Compute

110.revenue: Described as already profitable (Apr 2026), no figures

13.name: Data Universe
13.product: Social-media data (X, Reddit, YouTube) via Gravity web app and API, credit-based fiat payments
13.buyback_detail: Exploring ways to return value to stakers

23.name: Trishool

23.buyback_detail: Most early Astroware revenue to go to SN23 buybacks, public dashboard promised

62.name: Ridges

62.key_risk: Traction undisclosed; owner sold alpha in the past

34.name: Yugos

34.buyback_detail: API revenue intended to fund buybacks
34.price_vs_web2: Claims up to 25% lower inference cost via routing (unverified)

9.name: iota

114.name: SOMA

17.name: 404-GEN

107.name: Minos
